title: Differential equations
overview: Form and solve first-order differential equations by separating variables, using given initial conditions to find a particular solution. This guide turns the current syllabus outcomes into a connected revision sequence: learn the ideas, practise the method, then use the recall cards and checklist to diagnose what still needs work.
syllabusPoints: Translate rate-of-change statements into first-order differential equations.
Solve separable differential equations by integration.
Use an initial condition to find a particular solution.
Interpret constants and solutions in the modelling context.

definitions.definition: An equation involving a function and one or more of its derivatives.
A first-order equation that can be rearranged with all y terms with dy and all x terms with dx.
A family of solutions containing an arbitrary constant.
A known value such as y=y₀ when x=x₀ that selects one solution.
A constant k introduced when a rate is said to be proportional to a quantity.

sections.title: Forming the model
content: Translate phrases literally: 'rate of increase of y is proportional to y' gives dy/dt=ky; 'rate is proportional to the remaining amount' gives dM/dt=k(M₀−M). Choose the sign from whether the quantity increases or decreases.
bullets: Define variables and units before forming the equation.
A constant of proportionality is not automatically positive if its sign is already built into the model.

sections.title: Separating variables
content: From dy/dx=g(x)h(y), rearrange dy/h(y)=g(x)dx and integrate both sides. Separation must happen before integration. Use logarithmic absolute values where needed.
bullets: Never move dy/dx as though dy and dx were ordinary numbers without showing a valid separated form.
Check that dividing by h(y) has not discarded an equilibrium solution h(y)=0.

sections.title: Applying initial conditions
content: After integrating, include a constant and substitute the condition. Sometimes exponentiating produces a multiplicative constant more naturally. Leave an implicit solution if the question allows it; otherwise isolate y.
bullets: Apply the condition to the integrated equation, not the original derivative.
Use exact constants until the final numerical answer.

sections.title: Interpreting and checking
content: Differentiate the proposed solution to check it satisfies the differential equation and initial condition. In context, reject impossible branches and describe long-term behaviour, limiting values, monotonicity or the meaning of k.
bullets: A mathematical solution may violate physical restrictions such as mass≥0.
State units for time constants and rates.

examTips: State the proportionality equation before solving it.
Interpret the sign and units of the constant in the original context.
Show the mathematical setup and exact working before the final rounded answer; unsupported calculator output may not earn method marks.
commonMistakes: Using ln f(y) without an absolute value when the sign is not known.
Accepting a negative time, population or mass that is impossible in context.

quickRecall.question: What comes before integrating a separable equation?
quickRecall.answer: Rearrange so all y terms accompany dy and all x terms accompany dx.

quickRecall.question: What does an initial condition do?
quickRecall.answer: It determines the arbitrary constant and selects a particular solution.

quickRecall.question: What solution can be lost by dividing by h(y)?
quickRecall.answer: Any constant equilibrium solution satisfying h(y)=0.

quickRecall.question: How do you check a differential-equation solution?
quickRecall.answer: Differentiate it and substitute into both the equation and the initial condition.
